title.header: Stay-at-Home Parent Child Care Support Program

paragraph.header: Stay-at-home parent child care stipend program
paragraph.text: The term stay-at-home parent child care stipend program, means the program established under section 202.
The term stipend program means the stay-at-home parent child care support program.
The term benefit means a stay-at-home parent support benefit received under the support program.
The term eligible child means a child less than 3 years of age who does not participate in a child care program implemented under title I or title III.
The term parent means a stay-at-home individual who—

subparagraph.text: is the biological parent or legal guardian of an eligible child,
is the primary child care provider for an eligible child, and
has a household income of not to exceed—

clause.text: 75,000 for single individual, and
$150,000 for married individual filing jointly.

paragraph.text: The term Secretary means the Secretary of Health and Human Services.
The term Secretary of the Treasury means the Secretary of the Treasury or the Secretary of the Treasury’s delegate.
The term stay-at-home parent means a parent who chooses to directly care for an eligible child of such parent in such parent’s home.

section.header: Establishment of stay-at-home parent support benefit program
section.text: The Secretary shall establish the stay-at-home parent support program to provide financial assistance to parents who opt to directly care for their eligible children at home.

subsection.text: There is authorized to be appropriated $4,000,000,000 for each of the fiscal years 2024 through fiscal year 2034 to carry out this title.
Of the amount appropriated for a fiscal year—

paragraph.text: 95 percent shall be available for allocation under subsection (c) for the payment benefits,
3 percent shall be available to the Secretary of the Treasury for program administration, and
2 percent should be allocated to Secretary for program support and evaluation.

subsection.text: Funds shall be allocated among the States based on the proportion of children under age 3 in each State, adjusted for State median levels.
Except as otherwise provided in this Act, the stay-at-home parent child care stipend program shall be administered in the same manner as the child tax credit.
Eligible applicants shall annually self-certify their eligibility through the Internal Revenue Service as part of the individual’s annual income tax return.
Eligible applicants shall attest under penalty of perjury that the applicants meets the eligibility criteria to receive the stipend.

section.header: Responsibilities of the Secretary of the Treasury
section.text: The Secretary of the Treasury shall, with respect to the stay-at-home parent child care stipend program—

paragraph.text: modify relevant tax forms and systems to allow for claiming the stipend,
develop and implement systems for processing claims and distributing payments,
utilize existing programs and databases to verify eligibility based on income and dependent information,
distribute monthly advanced payments of the stipend using direct deposit,
verify eligible children and eligible parents,
process claims and distribute monthly payments,
conduct periodic audits to ensure program integrity,
establish procedures for handling overpayments and underpayments,
implement a system for reconciliation of payments through annual income tax returns, and
develop a process for mid-year changes in eligibility including, but not limited to, the birth of a child or change in income status.
develop and maintain education resources for parents, and

conduct research on the impact of the support program on child development and the well-being of the families of eligible children whose parents receive benefits, and coordinate the support program with other Federal early childhood programs.

section.text: In carrying out the support program, the Secretary and the Secretary of the Treasury shall—

paragraph.text: coordinate their activities,
work with the Social Security Administration, to verify the eligibility of children whose parents receive benefits, and

ensure that the Social Security Administration or the Secretary of the Treasury, as appropriate, shall— (A) send notifications to parents via letter and email, two months prior to their child's third birthday and one month prior to their child's third birthday, informing them that their eligibility is ending; and (B) assume responsibility for pausing payments upon the child's third birthday,

section.continuation-text: to verify the eligibility of children and parents participating in the support program so as to minimize waste, fraud, and abuse involving such program.

paragraph.text: Stipend recipients must report changes affecting eligibility within 30 days of the occurrence of such change. Changes affecting eligibility include enrollment in an eligible child care program, income exceeding threshold, and employment exceeding 10 hours per week.

The Internal Revenue Service shall provide multiple notification methods, including an online portal, mail, and phone, for reporting changes. Failure to report changes may result in penalties, including program disqualification.

subparagraph.text: If ineligibility is determined, the Internal Revenue Service will immediately cease future payments.
Overpayments will be recouped through the following methods:

clause.text: Reduction of future tax refunds.
Establishment of a repayment plan, not exceeding 12 months.
Deduction from other Federal tax benefits, subject to applicable laws.

subparagraph.text: Hardship exemptions may be granted for repayment on the basis for criteria established by the Internal Revenue Service.

paragraph.text: A 90-day grace period will be granted for repayment without interest or penalties if the parent voluntarily reports the change.
Stipend recipients may appeal recoupment decisions through the existing Internal Revenue Service appeals process.
Grounds for Appeal include—

subparagraph.text: Denial of eligibility.
Disagreement with benefit amount.
Recoupment decisions.
Program disqualification.
Stipend recipients must file an appeal within 60 days of receiving an adverse decision.
The Internal Revenue Service shall acknowledge receipt of appeals within 30 days.
A decision on the appeal shall be made within 90 days of receipt.

paragraph.text: Appeals may be submitted online, by mail, or by fax. The appeal must at least include the taxpayers identification information, specific reason for the appeal and supporting documentation.
An independent Internal Revenue Service appeals office will review each case. The officer may request additional information from the stipend recipient or relevant agencies.

Decisions of the Internal Revenue Service will be provided in writing, including the rationale. If the appeal is denied, information of further review options (including the Tax Court) shall be provided.

Benefits shall continue during the appeals process if the appeal is filed within 10 days of the adverse decision. If the appeal is denied, any benefits paid during the appeal process may be subject to recoupment.

Only information necessary for determining eligibility and administering the program shall be collected. Social Security numbers will be collected and used in accordance with section 7 of the Privacy Act.

Information collected shall be used solely for the administration of the stay-at-home parent child care stipend program and related tax administration purposes. o Data sharing between the Internal Revenue Service, Department of Health and Human Service, and Social Security Administration will be limited to information necessary for program administration and evaluation.

Personal data will be retained only for the duration necessary for program administration and in accordance with Internal Revenue Service records retention schedules. Secure data disposal methods will be used when destroying records.

Stipend recipients will provide informed consent for the collection and use of their data when applying for the program. Stipend recipients will have the right to request access to their data and correct any inaccuracies. Any third-party contractors handling program data will be contractually bound to the same privacy and security standards as Federal employees.

subsection.text: The Secretary of the Treasury, in collaboration with the Secretary of Health and Human Services, shall develop and implement a comprehensive outreach strategy within 6 months of the date of the enactment of this Act to inform families of options available for childcare.
At minimum, the strategy must include:

paragraph.text: Targeted messaging for potentially eligible families.
Partnerships with State and local agencies, community organizations and tax preparation services.
Multilingual materials and outreach effort including the use of multiple mediums of communication delivery including online, mail, and print.
Pursuant to such strategy, the Internal Revenue Service shall develop and maintain—

subparagraph.text: a dedicated website with program information, eligibility calculator, and answers to frequently asked questions (FAQ),
printed materials for distribution at Internal Revenue Service offices, community centers, and healthcare facilities, and
a toll-free help line for program inquiries.

paragraph.text: The Secretary shall develop—

subparagraph.text: resources on child development and effective home-based early learning practices, and

guides on transitioning children to formal childcare (including the programs authorized in this Act) or preschool programs (including making connections to relevant State agencies so parents have more of a seamless experience during the transition).

paragraph.text: The Internal Revenue Service shall provide training materials and guidance to tax preparers on the program and its interaction with other tax credits.
The Secretary of the Treasury shall conduct an annual awareness campaign prior to tax filing season to remind eligible parents about the program.

subsection.text: Not later than 6 months after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Secretary shall establish a set of evaluation metrics.
The Secretary shall establish a data collection system to gather information on these metrics.
The Secretary of shall conduct an annual evaluation of the program using these metrics and submit a report to Congress.
The Secretary of shall initiate a longitudinal study to track long-term outcome for child and families participating in the program.
Every 3 years the Government Accountability Office shall conduct an independent review of the program’s effectiveness based on these metrics.
Program Duration.—The stay-at-home parent support program is authorized for a period of 10 years from the date of enactment.

Not later than 18 months prior to the program’s expiration, the Secretary of the Treasury and the Secretary shall jointly submit a report to Congress on the program’s effectiveness and recommendations for continuation, modification or termination.
Congress shall review the program and vote on its reauthorization not later than 6 months prior to its expiration date.
If Congress decides not to reauthorize the program, the Secretary in collaboration with relevant agencies shall develop and implement a transition plan to phase out benefits over a 12-month period.

The stay-at-home parent support program benefit will be in addition to any child tax credit for which a family is eligible and not a substitute. Receipt of the stay-at-home parent child care stipend shall not affect child tax credit eligibility or amount.

For the purposes of calculating the earned income tax credit, the stay-at-home parent support program stipend will not be considered earned income or counted as income for determining earned income tax credit eligibility.

Individuals receiving the stay-at-home parent support program stipend with respect to any child are not be eligible for the child and dependent care credit with respect to such child for any taxable year during which such stipend is received.

subsection.header: Head Start and Early Head Start
subsection.text: Head Start and Early Head Start.—Receipt of the benefit will not affect eligibility for Head Start or Early Head Start programs”, although the decision to enroll in Head Start or Early Head Start for more than 10 hours a week will render a family ineligible for the benefit under this title.
States shall not take into account the stay-at-home parent support program stipend for purposes of determining TANF eligibility or benefit amounts.
The stay-at-home parent support program stipend shall not be counted as income for SNAP eligibility or benefit calculation purposes.
The stay-at-home parent support program stipend shall not be counted as income for determining eligibility for Medicaid or the Children’s Health Insurance Program CHIP.
The stay-at-home parent support program stipend shall not be counted as income for determining eligibility for Federal housing assistance programs.

The Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary, and other relevant agency heads shall conduct an annual review of the program’s interaction with other Federal benefits and tax credits, and report to Congress any unintended consequences or recommended adjustments.

paragraph.text: Eligible stay-at-home parents will receive $300 per month per eligible child.
The Secretary of the Treasury shall have the authority to adjust the benefit amount annually based on cost-of-living increases, subject to Congressional approval.

The Internal Revenue Service shall distribute payments monthly through accessible payment methods to families including but not limited to direct deposit to the bank account designated by the parent, prepaid debit cards for parents without bank accounts, paper checks as a last report if neither of the above options is feasible. Payments shall be made on a set date each month, to be determined by the Secretary of the Treasury.
The first payment shall be made within 30 days of the eligibility determination or recertification.

Benefits will continue until the eligible child reaches the age of 3 or enters another childcare program funded by the Child Care for America Grant Program or the program under title III for more than 10 hours a week, whichever comes first.
Annual recertification shall be completed not later than the due date (determined without regard to any extensions) for the income tax return of the eligible recipient of the benefits.
The Internal Revenue Service shall provide multiple reminders to parents about the recertification requirement, including but not limited to the following:

subparagraph.text: Notices with monthly benefit payments starting three months before the tax filing deadline.
Email and text message reminders if parents have opted in for such communications.

paragraph.text: Parents who fail to recertify by the deadline may have their benefits suspended 30 days after the due date referred to in subsection (c)(2).
If recertification is completed within 90 days after the deadline:

subparagraph.text: Benefits shall be reinstated prospectively from the date of recertification.
Any missed payments due to late recertification shall be paid retroactively in a lump sum within one year after the original deadline.

paragraph.text: The Internal Revenue Service shall provide multiple channels for recertification including but not limited to:

subparagraph.text: Automatic recertification on income tax returns other relevant tax documents during tax filing season.
A process for recertification and disclosure of change of status that may make a parent ineligible throughout the calendar year in the form of a website or other accessible service delivery channel.

paragraph.text: Benefits will continue until the eligible child reaches the age of 3 or enters another childcare program funded by the Child Care for America Grant Program or the program under title III for more than 10 hours a week, whichever comes first:

subparagraph.text: Child enrolling in a childcare program for more than 10 hours a week that makes them ineligible for the benefit.
Changes in income affecting eligibility.

paragraph.header: On-line portal and dedicated phone line
paragraph.text: The Internal Revenue Service shall provide an online portal and a dedicated phone line for reporting changes.
Benefits shall be adjusted or terminated as appropriate based on reported changes, effective from the month following the change.
Benefit recipients will have the right to appeal decisions regarding benefit amounts, eligibility determinations or recoupment of overpayments.
Appeals must be filed within 60 days of receiving notice of the decision.
The Internal Revenue Service shall establish an expedited review process for such appeals.
The Internal Revenue Service shall implement robust security measures to prevent unauthorized access to payment information.
The Internal Revenue Service shall conduct regular audits to identify and prevent fraudulent claims.
Penalties for fraudulent claims shall include repayment of benefits, fines and potential criminal prosecution.

subsection.text: The Secretary of the Treasury shall submit an annual report to Congress describing the number of families receiving the benefit, total amount distributed and any significant issues or challenges in benefit distribution.

The Secretary of the Treasury and the Secretary shall conduct an annual evaluation of the payment mechanism and benefit structure. The evaluation must also assess the efficiency of benefit distribution, impact on eligible families and any recommended improvements.

title.header: Kin Care: Family, Friend, and Neighbor (FFN) Care Program

paragraph.text: the term FFN provider means an individual who provides childcare services to eligible children in a home setting and is not required to be licensed under State law;
the term eligible FFN provider means a FFN provider who meets the requirements set forth in this section and is registered with the State law; and
the term FFN care means child care services provided by an eligible FFN provider.

section.text: There is authorized to be appropriated $5,000,000,000 annually for fiscal years 2024 through 2034 to carry out this title, to be allocated as follows:

paragraph.text: 75 percent for direct payments to verified FFN provider;
15 percent for State-level program administration and support services;
8 percent for Federal administration, including the development and maintenance of a national FFN database and verification system; and
2 percent for research, evaluation, and continuous improvement initiatives.

section.header: Parent roles and responsibilities in the FFN Care Program

paragraph.text: To be eligible for the FFN Care Program, a parent shall meet income eligibility requirements (up to 100 percent of State median income).
An eligible parent shall—

subparagraph.text: complete the FFN care subsidy application through the Kin Care Interface within 30 days of seeking care; and
provide accurate and complete information, including—

clause.text: proof of income;
number and ages of children needing care; and
hours of care needed.

paragraph.text: An eligible parent shall—

subparagraph.text: nominate their FFN provider to the Interface for verification, after which time FFN providers may voluntarily join the Interface and seek verification as set out in the provider section; and
confirm the care arrangement with the chosen provider through the Kin Care Interface within 5 days of selection.

paragraph.text: The parent shall—

subparagraph.text: enter into a standard consent agreement with the FFN provider within 7 days of selection, outlining—

clause.text: care schedule; and
expectations for both parties; and

subparagraph.text: enter into a written agreement with the FFN provider within 7 days of selection, outlining—

clause.text: care schedule;
compensation details;
expectations for both parties; and
upload the signed agreement to the Kin Care Interface within 3 days of signing.

paragraph.text: For care in the child's home, the parent shall—

subparagraph.text: provide written confirmation about the suitability of their home for childcare within 5 days of provider selection;
complete a home safety checklist provided through the Kin Care Interface within 10 days of provider selection; and
allow for virtual or in-person safety assessments of the home environment as required by the State agency.
The parent shall verify child attendance through the Kin Care Interface on a weekly basis, within 2 days of the end of each care week.
The parent shall—

clause.text: complete semi-annual care quality surveys through the Kin Care Interface;
provide additional feedback or concerns as they arise, within 24 hours for urgent matters; and
any major safety incidents while the child is in FFN care, with major safety incidents defined as hospitalization resulting from provider neglect, or any incident leading to suspicion of child abuse.

subparagraph.text: The parent shall report the following changes within 10 days of occurrence—

clause.text: income changes that may affect eligibility;
employment or education/training status changes;
family size or composition changes; and
relocation or contact information updates.

subparagraph.text: The parent shall—

clause.text: participate in annual re-certification processes;
completing all required documentation within 30 days of request;
cooperate with any investigations or follow-ups regarding reported incidents or concerns within the timeframe specified by the investigating agency; and
allow for and facilitate visits by State agency representatives if care is provided in the child’s home.

subparagraph.text: The parent shall complete any required parent orientation or training modules within 30 days of enrollment in the FFN care program.
The parent shall—

clause.text: provide up-to-date immunization records for the child to the provider within 7 days of care commencement or any updates; and
inform the provider of any health concerns, allergies, or special needs of the child before care begins and as new information arises.

subparagraph.text: The parent shall—

clause.text: adhere to all rules and regulations of the FFN care program as outlined in the parent handbook; and
acknowledge that failure to comply with these responsibilities may result in termination from the program or repayment of subsidies.

section.header: FFN provider responsibilities in the Kin Care Program

paragraph.text: To be eligible as an FFN provider, an individual shall—

subparagraph.text: be at least 18 years old as of the date of application;
be a grandparent, aunt or uncle of the child;
not have any criminal record involving violent offenses, nor prior credible child abuse findings, nor be present on any sex offender registry; and

after the first three years of the Kin Care program, the Secretary may, in consultation with relevant stakeholders, elect to extend eligibility to additional family members, trusted friends, and trusted neighbors.

A FFN caregiver currently registered as a subsidy-receiving provider via the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 1990 shall discontinue their participation upon being verified to be part of the Kin Care program and beginning to receive payments via the Kin Care program.
FFN caregivers who are not eligible for the Kin Care program but who are eligible for payment under CCDBG may continue to participate in that program.
In the case that the Secretary elects to extend eligibility for the Kin Care program to cover all those FFN providers eligible under CCDBG, the relevant sections of CCDBG are to be repealed.

paragraph.text: The provider shall—

subparagraph.text: complete the online registration form through the Kin Care Interface within 30 days of deciding to become an FFN provider;
provide accurate and complete information as required by the Kin Care Interface; and
submit to comprehensive background checks within 10 days of registration.

paragraph.text: The provider shall—

subparagraph.text: for care in provider’s home—

clause.text: submit clear, recent photos or a video tour of all areas used for child care within 7 days of registration;
participate in a virtual safety assessment within 14 days of registration; and
allow for an in-person home visit within 30 days of approval.

subparagraph.text: for care in child’s home—

clause.text: sign an agreement to maintain safe practices in the child’s home within 5 days of registration; and
schedule a home familiarization visit with the family within 10 days of registration.

subparagraph.text: The provider shall—

clause.text: complete 20 hours of mandatory online health and safety training within 30 days of registration;
achieve a minimum score of 80 percent on module quizzes to progress; and
complete a standardized knowledge assessment within 7 days of completing all training modules.

subparagraph.text: The provider shall—

clause.text: complete 10 hours of approved ongoing training annually;
obtain and maintain certification in pediatric first aid and CPR; and
submit certificates of completion for all training through the Kin Care Interface within 7 days of completion.

subparagraph.text: The provider shall—

clause.text: care for no more than 6 children at a time, including the provider’s own children under age 13;
maintain a daily log of all children in care;
maintain direct sight or sound supervision of all children at all times; and
make reasonable efforts to implement daily activities that support child's development and early learning, including reading and outdoor play.

subparagraph.text: The provider shall—

clause.text: maintain a smoke-free environment at all times during hours of operation;
ensure all areas used for child care are free from visible safety hazards;
implement safe sleep practices for infants and toddlers;
store all medications and hazardous materials in locked containers out of children's reach;
maintain a fully stocked first aid kit and emergency preparedness plan; and
have and maintain working carbon monoxide and smoke detectors and fire extinguisher(s).

subparagraph.text: If providing meals, the provider shall—

clause.text: develop weekly meal plans that meet USDA Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) guidelines;
maintain current food handler's certification if preparing meals; and
follow proper food safety and hygiene practices.
The provider shall submit weekly care hours through the Kin Care Interface within 2 days of the end of each care week.
The provider shall report all income from child care services on annual tax returns.
The provider shall—

subclause.text: report any injuries requiring medical attention within 24 hours of occurrence; and
report any suspected child abuse or neglect immediately to the appropriate authorities and the State agency.

clause.text: The provider shall—

subclause.text: participate in annual re-verification process, completing all requirements within 30 days of notification;
be available for random virtual check-ins during declared hours of operation; and
allow for both announced and unannounced in-person visits by State agency representatives.

section.header: child care practices for family, friend, and neighbor providers

paragraph.text: An FFN provider shall not care for more than 4children at any given time, including the provider's own children under the age of 13.
The provider shall indicate via the Kin Care Interface the number, age, and initials of children cared for each day.
The provider shall ensure that no more than 2 children under the age of 2 are in care at any time.
For children with special needs, the provider shall adjust ratios as required by the child's individual care plan, in consultation with the child's parents and Kin Care Program administrators.

section.header: FFN provider verification procedures and ongoing monitoring

subsection.header: Development and maintenance of the Kin Care interface

paragraph.text: The Secretary shall—

subparagraph.text: contract with a reputable software development firm to create the Kin Care Interface within 100 days after the date of the enactment of this Act;
ensure the interface is web-based and includes a mobile application version;
incorporate robust security measures, including end-to-end encryption and multi-factor authentication;
develop user-friendly interfaces for providers, parents, and State administrators;
be prepared to launch the Interface within one year of passage of this Act;
collect only minimum required data to meet the intent and requirements of this Act; and

ensure that at launch, the interface is available in at least English and Spanish, and that it is made available in all languages spoken by at least 1 percent of the U.S. population within one year of launch, and all languages spoken by at least 0.1 percent of the U.S. population within two years of launch.

paragraph.text: The Kin Care Interface shall include—

subparagraph.text: provider registration and profile management capabilities;
document upload capabilities for ID’s, background check results, and training certificates;
a secure messaging system between providers, parents, and State administrators;
an automated alert system for expired documents or pending re-verifications;
integration with State and Federal databases for background check verificationl;
a secure payment system, including a method for providing compensation to individuals who, at registration, lack a bank account;
capabilities for States or the Department to design or upload training modules, and for providers to complete said modules; and
all other functionalities as needed to carry out the provisions of this Act.

paragraph.text: The Secretary shall—

subparagraph.text: conduct quarterly system updates to address bugs and improve functionality;
perform annual security audits and penetration testing; and
maintain a 24/7 technical support helpline for users and State administrators.
The Secretary shall—

clause.text: specify acceptable forms of government-issued photo ID;
set requirements for third-party identity verification services; and
define acceptable documents for address confirmation, such as utility bills no older than 60 days.

subparagraph.text: The Secretary shall—

clause.text: establish a comprehensive list of disqualifying offenses; and
set standards for an appeals process for providers with concerning but non-disqualifying results.

subparagraph.text: The Secretary shall—

clause.text: develop a standardized checklist for virtual safety assessments which includes items necessary to ensure safety but do not present an undue burden to providers;
establish means for providers to remedy any concerns and receive a timely re-assessment; and
establish minimum photo/video documentation requirements for provider's home assessments.

subparagraph.text: The Secretary shall—

clause.text: develop a mandatory online health and safety training curriculum; and
require training to be available in at least 5 languages.

subparagraph.text: The Secretary shall—

clause.text: set a 30-day window for annual re-verification completion; and
establish required components of re-verification.

subparagraph.text: The Secretary shall—

clause.text: establish partnerships with State law enforcement agencies for real-time arrest notifications for violent offenses, child abuse offenses, or offenses resulting in addition to sex offender registries. No such partnerships shall be construed by the Secretary or States as means to provide law enforcement agencies with information outside the relevant scope of the Kin Care program, notwithstanding information sharing required under existing State and Federal law;
develop a system for providers to self-report new criminal charges or child protective services involvement within 48 hours; and
set a 3-year cycle for full background check renewals.

subparagraph.text: The Secretary shall—

clause.text: develop a standardized incident report form; and
establish a tiered response system based on incident severity.

paragraph.text: The Secretary shall—

subparagraph.text: establish a graduated system of enforcement actions; and
develop an appeals process for providers facing adverse actions.

subsection.text: Each State agency shall—

paragraph.text: designate a State-level administrator to oversee the Kin Care Interface;
review all provider registrations within 10 business days of submission;
conduct identity verification processes within specified timeframes;
administer background checks according to Federal guidelines;
conduct care setting verifications for both provider's home and child's home care settings;
verify completion of required training and education by providers;
manage the annual re-verification process for providers;
conduct random virtual check-ins with 5 percent of approved providers each month;
maintain a system for continuous background check monitoring;
manage the parent feedback system and respond to concerns in a timely manner;
investigate and respond to reported incidents according to the tiered response system;
implement compliance and enforcement actions as necessary;
provide quality improvement support to providers as needed;
submit required reports to the Secretary on program operations and outcomes;
establish a localized schedule of payment rates, and ensure timely payment to providers (no more than five business days after the end of a payment period);
ensure all State Kin Care Interface materials and related materials are available in, at minimum, all languages spoken by more than 1 percent of the population in their State;
establish a process for parents and providers to offer feedback, complaints and concerns regarding monitoring, enforcement and program operations; and

create or utilize an existing FFN advisory or governance structure to give input and oversee implementation; this committee must be provided data and information regarding the program including numbers of participants and participant complaints/concerns with program operations.
The Secretary shall establish a system for regular reporting and evaluation of the FFN Provider Verification Procedures and Ongoing Monitoring processes.
State agencies shall submit monthly and quarterly reports as specified by the Secretary.
The Secretary shall conduct an annual evaluation of the effectiveness of these procedures and make recommendations for improvements as necessary.
The States and Secretary shall gather participant experience data to understand barriers, administrative and paperwork burdens, use of technology challenges, etc., that may be limiting participation.
The Secretary shall establish a national base rate for FFN care that is no less than 75 percent of the State's rate for licensed family child care homes.
States may adjust the base rate to account for—

subparagraph.text: geographic cost of living differences;
number and ages of children in care;
non-traditional hours care (evenings, weekends, overnight);
care for children with special needs;
provider education and training levels; and
the Secretary shall review and update the national base rate annually to reflect changes in the cost of living and child care market rates.

paragraph.text: FFN providers shall submit number of weekly hours of service through the Kin Care Interface within 2 days of the end of each care week.
The Kin Care Interface shall automatically calculate payment amounts based on—

subparagraph.text: reported hours;
approved rate for the provider; and
any adjustments for non-traditional hours, special needs care, or other adjustments.

paragraph.text: Parents shall verify reports via the Kin Care Interface within a reasonable timeframe.
FFN providers shall submit weekly attendance reports through the Kin Care Interface within 2 days of the end of each care week.
The Kin Care Interface shall automatically calculate payment amounts based on—

subparagraph.text: reported attendance;
approved rate for the provider;
any adjustments for non-traditional hours or special needs care.

paragraph.text: Parents shall verify the attendance reports within 1 day of submission by the provider.
The State agency shall process payments within 3 business days of verified submission.
The Kin Care Interface shall generate a detailed payment Statement for each pay period, accessible to both the provider and the State agency.
In cases of overpayment due to error or misreporting—

subparagraph.text: the State agency shall notify the provider within 5 business days of discovery; and
recovery of overpayments shall be through reduced future payments, not to exceed 10 percent of each payment until the overpayment is recovered.

paragraph.text: In cases of underpayment, The State agency shall issue an additional payment to correct the underpayment within 5 business days of discovery.

subsection.header: Payment for training and professional development

paragraph.text: FFN providers shall be compensated at their regular rate for time spent in required training and professional development activities, which providers shall record as normal hours of service.
The State agency shall pay for any fees associated with required training courses or materials.
The Kin Care Interface shall generate annual tax documents (e.g., 1099 forms) for FFN providers by January 31st of each year.
FFN providers shall be responsible for reporting all income and paying applicable taxes.
FFN providers may file a payment dispute through the Kin Care Interface within 30 days of the payment date.
The State agency shall investigate and resolve payment disputes within 10 business days of filing.
If the dispute is not resolved to the provider's satisfaction, they may appeal to a designated State appeal board within 15 days of the State agency's decision.
The Secretary shall establish comprehensive data protection standards for the Kin Care Interface, including—

subparagraph.text: end-to-end encryption for all data transmissions;
multi-factor authentication for user access; and
regular security audits and penetration testing.

paragraph.text: All data stored in the Kin Care Interface shall be classified according to sensitivity level and protected accordingly.
The Kin Care Interface shall collect only information necessary for program administration and evaluation.
Personal identifying information shall be used solely for the purposes of:

subparagraph.text: verifying eligibility;
facilitating payments;
conducting background checks; and
communicating with program participants.

paragraph.text: Data sharing between State agencies and the Federal Government shall be governed by formal data sharing agreements.
Any data shared for research purposes shall be de-identified to protect individual privacy.

subsection.text: FFN providers and parents shall have the right to—

paragraph.text: access their personal data stored in the Kin Care Interface;
request corrections to inaccurate data; and
receive notification of any data breaches affecting their information within 72 hours.
The Secretary shall establish data retention schedules for different types of data collected.
Data shall be securely disposed of when no longer necessary, using methods that prevent reconstruction.

section.header: Transition to licensed family child care

paragraph.text: The Secretary shall establish a Transition Support Program to assist FFN providers in voluntarily becoming licensed family child care providers.
The program shall include—

subparagraph.text: guidance on State licensing requirements;
financial assistance for meeting licensing standards; and
mentorship from experienced licensed providers.

subsection.text: FFN providers who have participated in the Kin Care Program for at least one year shall be eligible for the Transition Support Program.
Eligible providers may receive grants of up to $5,000 to cover costs associated with meeting licensing requirements, including—

paragraph.text: home modifications for safety compliance;
purchase of required equipment and materials; and
fees for required training and certifications.

subsection.text: The State agency shall provide specialized training to support the transition, including—

paragraph.text: business management for family child care;
advanced child development courses; and
curriculum planning and implementation.

subsection.text: The State agency shall assign a dedicated licensing navigator to each transitioning provider to assist with the licensing application and inspection process.

section.header: Supports for serving children with special needs

paragraph.text: The Secretary shall develop a specialized training module for FFN providers caring for children with special needs.
The training shall cover—

subparagraph.text: understanding common disabilities and developmental delays;
adapting activities and environments;
collaborating with early intervention specialists; and
supporting families of children with special needs.

subsection.text: FFN providers caring for children with diagnosed special needs shall receive an enhanced payment rate, to be determined by the State agency based on the child's specific needs.
FFN providers may apply for grants of up to $1,000 annually to purchase specialized equipment or materials needed to care for children with special needs.
The State agency shall facilitate a peer support network for FFN providers caring for children with special needs.

section.header: Collaboration with other early childhood programs

paragraph.text: State agencies shall establish formal coordination agreements with—

subparagraph.text: Early Head Start and Head Start programs;
State pre-kindergarten programs;
part C early intervention programs under IDEAl; and
State Child Care Resource and Referral Agencies.

paragraph.text: The Secretary shall encourage and facilitate shared services among Kin Care and other early childhood programs, including—

subparagraph.text: joint professional development opportunities;
shared curriculum resources; and
coordinated developmental screening services.

paragraph.text: State agencies shall develop protocols to support children's transitions between FFN care and other early childhood programs.
The Secretary shall establish guidelines for appropriate data sharing between Kin Care and other early childhood programs to support coordinated services and program evaluation.

subsection.text: The Secretary shall conduct an annual evaluation of the Kin Care Program, assessing—

paragraph.text: program reach and participation rates;
care practices;
family outcomes, including parental employment and economic stability; and
provider outcomes, including job satisfaction and financial stability.

subsection.text: The Secretary shall commission a 10-year longitudinal study to assess the long-term impacts of participation in FFN care through the Kin Care Program.
The Secretary shall establish a research grant program to study innovative approaches to supporting and enhancing FFN care.

The Kin Care Interface shall include mechanisms for ongoing data collection to support evaluation and research efforts. o State agencies shall be required to participate in all national evaluation efforts as a condition of receiving Kin Care Program funds.
The Secretary shall ensure wide dissemination of research findings through—

paragraph.text: annual reports to Congress;
peer-reviewed journal publications;
presentations at national conferences; and
easily accessible summaries on the program website.
The Secretary shall establish a process for using evaluation and research findings to continuously improve the Kin Care Program.
This process shall include annual review and updating of program policies and practices based on the latest evidence.

section.header: Community engagement for the Kin Care Program

subsection.header: Establishment of local community advisory boards

paragraph.text: Each State agency shall establish Local Community Advisory Boards (LCABs) to provide input on Kin Care Program implementation and operation. The State may establish a reasonable minimum population size for establishing LCABs, or have one LCAB cover multiple jurisdictions if necessary.
Each LCAB shall consist of—

subparagraph.text: at least two FFN providers participating in the Kin Care Program;
at least two parents utilizing FFN care through the Kin Care Program;
one representative from the local child care resource and referral agency;
one early childhood education expert from a local college or university;
one representative from a local community-based organization serving families;
one representative from the local business community;
one representative from the local government; and
one expert from a local (or, if no local, Statewide) FFN-serving organization”.
The State agency shall develop a fair and transparent process for appointing LCAB members.
Members shall serve staggered three-year terms, with the possibility of reappointment for one additional term.

paragraph.text: Each LCAB shall—

subparagraph.text: meet at least quarterly to review local Kin Care Program implementation;
provide recommendations to the State agency on program improvements;
assist in identifying and addressing barriers to program participation;
support community outreach efforts; and
submit an annual report to the State agency summarizing their activities and recommendations.

paragraph.text: The State agency shall establish formal partnerships with community organizations to support the Kin Care Program, including but not limited to—

subparagraph.text: faith-based organizations;
cultural and ethnic community groups;
public libraries;
community centers;
local health departments;
school districts; and
local businesses.

paragraph.text: Each partnership shall be formalized through a written agreement that outlines—

subparagraph.text: the roles and responsibilities of each party;
the resources each party will contribute;
the expected outcomes of the partnership; and
the duration of the partnership and conditions for renewal.

paragraph.text: Community partnerships shall focus on—

subparagraph.text: outreach to potential FFN providers and families;
providing venues for training and support group meetings;
offering complementary services to Kin Care Program participants;
assisting with culturally and linguistically appropriate program implementation; and
supporting program evaluation efforts.

paragraph.text: The State agency shall develop and implement a comprehensive community outreach and engagement plan that includes—

subparagraph.text: multilingual marketing materials about the Kin Care Program;
social media campaigns targeting potential FFN providers and families;
information sessions at community events and gatherings;
door-to-door outreach in targeted neighborhoods;
partnerships with local media outlets, including ethnic media; and
a dedicated community liaison position within the State agency.

paragraph.text: The State agency shall ensure that all outreach efforts are culturally responsive and appropriate for the diverse communities served by the Kin Care Program.
The State agency shall utilize technology to enhance community engagement, including—

subparagraph.text: a mobile-friendly website with program information and resources;
text message reminders and updates for program participants;
virtual information sessions and webinars; and
an online community forum for FFN providers and families.

paragraph.text: The State agency shall establish multiple channels for ongoing community feedback, including—

subparagraph.text: an annual community survey on the Kin Care Program;
focus groups with diverse stakeholders;
a dedicated email address and phone line for community input; and
public comment periods for proposed program changes.

paragraph.text: The State agency shall—

subparagraph.text: Review all community feedback on a quarterly basis;
Incorporate relevant feedback into program improvement efforts; and
provide public responses to major themes in community feedback.

paragraph.text: The State agency shall collaborate with community partners to offer—

subparagraph.text: localized training sessions for FFN providers;
peer support groups in community settings;
family engagement activities; and
community-based child development workshops for parents and FFN providers.
The State agency shall include a community engagement section in its annual report to the Secretary, detailing—

clause.text: LCAB activities and recommendations;
outcomes of community partnerships;
reach and impact of outreach efforts;
summary of community feedback received; and
changes made to the program based on community input.

subparagraph.text: The Secretary shall evaluate the effectiveness of community engagement efforts as part of the annual Kin Care Program evaluation.
The State agency shall allocate at least 5 percent of its Kin Care Program administrative budget to community engagement activities.
The Secretary shall provide supplemental grants to State agencies demonstrating innovative and effective community engagement strategies.

The Secretary shall establish a fund of $1,000,000 annually to issue grants to trusted FFN serving organizations in order for those organizations to conduct outreach, support enrollment in the program, and support FFN providers. The application for such a Fund shall be streamlined and simplified to the maximum extent possible under Federal law.
